Benjamin "Bibi" Netanyahu (born 21 October 1949) is an Israeli politician and diplomat who has served as prime minister of Israel since 2022. Having previously held office from 1996 to 1999 and from 2009 to 2021, Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister.

By the time Benjamin Netanyahu reached the defining moment, the preparation was decades old. Born in Tel Aviv, Netanyahu was raised in West Jerusalem and the United States. He returned to Israel in 1967 to join the Israel Defense Forces and served in the Sayeret Matkal special forces.

The rise of Benjamin Netanyahu was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. In 1972, he returned to the US, and after graduating from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Netanyahu worked for the Boston Consulting Group. Between 1984 and 1988 Netanyahu was Israel's ambassador to the United Nations.

Setbacks came early for Benjamin Netanyahu, and the response to them is the real story. Netanyahu rose to prominence after his election as chair of Likud in 1993, becoming leader of the opposition. In the 1996 general election, Netanyahu became the first Israeli prime minister elected directly by popular vote.

The legacy of Benjamin Netanyahu outlived the circumstances that produced it. Netanyahu was defeated in the 1999 election and entered the private sector. He served as minister of foreign affairs and finance, initiating economic reforms, before resigning over the Gaza disengagement plan.

Few lives travel as far as that of Benjamin Netanyahu, and the distance is the point. Netanyahu returned to lead Likud in 2005, leading the opposition between 2006 and 2009. After the 2009 legislative election, Netanyahu formed a coalition and became prime minister again.

The childhood of Benjamin Netanyahu contains the adult in small print. Netanyahu made his closeness to Donald Trump central to his appeal from 2016. During Trump's first presidency, the US recognized Jerusalem as capital of Israel, Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights, and brokered the Abraham Accords between Israel and the Arab world.

Money, luck and timing all played their parts in the life of Benjamin Netanyahu — in that order. Netanyahu was criticized for expanding Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, deemed illegal under international law. In 2019, Netanyahu was indicted on charges of breach of trust, bribery and fraud, and relinquished all ministerial posts except prime minister.

The turning point in the life of Benjamin Netanyahu looked like a failure at the time. The 2018–2022 Israeli political crisis resulted in a rotation agreement between Netanyahu and Benny Gantz. In June 2021, Netanyahu was removed as prime minister, before returning after the 2022 election.

Every biography of Benjamin Netanyahu has to pass through the years that were quietly lost. Netanyahu's governments have been criticized for perceived democratic backsliding and an alleged shift toward authoritarianism. His coalition's 2023 judicial reform proposals sparked mass protests, while the October 7 Hamas-led attacks and the ensuing Gaza war led to nationwide protests over the security lapses and the failure to secure the Israeli hostages' return.

The education of Benjamin Netanyahu happened mostly outside any school. In 2024, Israel exchanged strikes with Iran, while Netanyahu ordered invasions of Lebanon and Syria and survived an assassination attempt in October. Netanyahu's government has been orchestrating the Gaza genocide, culminating in the South Africa v.

What Benjamin Netanyahu wanted at the start and what Benjamin Netanyahu got are not the same thing, and that gap is the story. Israel case before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in December 2023. The International Criminal Court (ICC) issued an arrest warrant in November 2024 for Netanyahu for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity as part of the ICC investigation in Palestine.

The defining trait of Benjamin Netanyahu was not talent — it was the refusal to stop. His mother, Tzila Segal, was born in Petah Tikva in the Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem—her family had migrated from Minneapolis in 1911, having relocated there from Lithuania in the 1870s—and studied law at Gray's Inn, London. His father, Warsaw-born Benzion Netanyahu (né Mileikowsky), was a historian specializing in the Jewish Golden Age of Spain.

Those who met Benjamin Netanyahu at the peak describe someone still running on the early hunger. When Netanyahu's father immigrated to Mandatory Palestine, he adopted the Hebrew surname "Netanyahu", meaning "God has given". His family is predominantly Ashkenazi, but he has said that a DNA test revealed some Sephardic ancestry.

The private years of Benjamin Netanyahu explain the public decades better than any speech. His evaluation by his 6th-grade teacher Ruth Rubenstein says that Netanyahu was courteous, polite, and helpful; "responsible and punctual"; and friendly, disciplined, cheerful, brave, active, and obedient. Between 1956 and 1958, and from 1963 to 1967, his family lived in the United States in Cheltenham Township, Pennsylvania, while Benzion Netanyahu taught at Dropsie College.

The family Benjamin Netanyahu came from matters more than the legends admit. Benjamin graduated from Cheltenham High School and was active in the debate club, chess club, and soccer. He and his brother Yonatan grew dissatisfied with what they saw as the superficial way of life in the area, including the prevalent youth counterculture movement and the liberal sensibilities of the Reform synagogue, Temple Judea of Philadelphia, that the family attended.

The first real success of Benjamin Netanyahu arrived later than anyone expected, and changed everything. After graduating from high school in 1967, Netanyahu returned to Israel to enlist in the Israel Defense Forces. He trained as a combat soldier and served for five years in a special forces unit of the IDF, Sayeret Matkal.

The last chapter of Benjamin Netanyahu was written long after the fame. He took part in numerous cross-border raids during the 1967–70 War of Attrition, including the March 1968 Battle of Karameh, when the IDF attacked Jordan to capture PLO leader Yasser Arafat but were repulsed with heavy casualties. He was involved in many other missions, including the 1968 Israeli raid on Lebanon and the rescue of the hijacked Sabena Flight 571 in May 1972, during which he was shot in the shoulder.

The whole life of Benjamin Netanyahu reads like a single decision repeated. Following his discharge, he left to study in the United States but returned in October 1973 to serve in the Yom Kippur War. Netanyahu returned to the United States in late 1972 to study architecture at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

Between the birth and the legend of Benjamin Netanyahu lie the years that actually decide it. After returning to Israel to fight in the Yom Kippur War, he returned to the United States and, under the name Ben Nitay, completed a Bachelor of Science in architecture in February 1975. In 1976 he earned a master's degree from the MIT Sloan School of Management.

The reputation of Benjamin Netanyahu was built in the middle, not at the edges. His studies were broken off by the death of his brother, Yonatan, who led the Entebbe raid. At MIT, Netanyahu studied a double-load while taking courses at Harvard University, completing his bachelor's degree in architecture in two and a half years, despite taking a break to fight in the Yom Kippur War.

Somebody like Benjamin Netanyahu should not have made it — that is exactly why the story survives. At that time he changed his name to Benjamin "Ben" Nitai (Nitai, a reference to both Mount Nitai and the eponymous Jewish sage Nittai of Arbela, a pen name his father often used). Years later, in an interview with the media, Netanyahu clarified that he decided to do so to make it easier for Americans to pronounce his name.

The life of Benjamin Netanyahu begins far from where the story usually starts. This fact has been used by his political rivals to accuse him indirectly of a lack of Israeli national identity and loyalty. Netanyahu worked as an economic consultant for the Boston Consulting Group in Boston, Massachusetts, working at the company between 1976 and 1978.

Benjamin Netanyahu was not born famous — the early years shaped everything that followed. At the Boston Consulting Group, he was a colleague of Mitt Romney, with whom he formed a lasting friendship. Romney described Netanyahu at the time as "a strong personality with a distinct point of view".

To understand where Benjamin Netanyahu ended up, start with where Benjamin Netanyahu began. Netanyahu said that their "easy communication" was a result of "B.C.G.'s intellectually rigorous boot camp". Between 1978 and 1980, he ran the Jonathan Netanyahu Anti-Terror Institute, a non-governmental organization devoted to the study of terrorism.

The road from the beginning to the peak of Benjamin Netanyahu ran through years nobody filmed. From 1980 to 1982, he was director of marketing for Rim Industries in Jerusalem. Moshe Arens appointed him as his Deputy Chief of Mission at the Israeli Embassy in Washington, D.C., while Arens was ambassador to the United States, a position he held from 1982 until 1984.

Each stage of the life of Benjamin Netanyahu made the next stage possible. During the 1982 Lebanon War, he was called up for reserve duty in Sayeret Matkal and requested to be released from service, preferring to remain in the US and serve as a spokesperson for Israel in the wake of harsh international criticism of the war. He presented Israel's case to the media during the war and established a highly efficient public relations system in the Israeli embassy.

The people who knew Benjamin Netanyahu young describe someone already restless. Between 1984 and 1988, Netanyahu served as the Israeli ambassador to the United Nations. Also during the 1980s, Netanyahu became friends with Fred Trump, the father of future U.S. president Donald Trump.

What Benjamin Netanyahu built in the middle years is what the name still stands for. Prior to the 1988 Israeli legislative election, Netanyahu returned to Israel and joined the Likud party. In the Likud's internal elections, Netanyahu was placed fifth on the party list.

By the time Benjamin Netanyahu reached the defining moment, the preparation was decades old. Later on he was elected as a Knesset member of the 12th Knesset, and was appointed as a deputy of the foreign minister Moshe Arens, and later on David Levy. Netanyahu and Levy did not cooperate and the rivalry between the two only intensified afterwards.

The rise of Benjamin Netanyahu was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. During the Gulf War in early 1991, the English-fluent Netanyahu emerged as the principal spokesman for Israel in media interviews on CNN and other news outlets. During the Madrid Conference of 1991 Netanyahu was a member of the Israeli delegation headed by Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir.

Setbacks came early for Benjamin Netanyahu, and the response to them is the real story. After the Madrid Conference Netanyahu was appointed as Deputy Minister in the Israeli Prime Minister's Office. Shamir retired from politics shortly after the Likud's defeat in the 1992 elections.

The legacy of Benjamin Netanyahu outlived the circumstances that produced it. Following the assassination of Yitzhak Rabin at the end of a rally in support of the Oslo Accords, Rabin's temporary successor Shimon Peres decided to call early elections in order to give the government a mandate to advance the peace process. Netanyahu was the Likud's candidate for prime minister in the 1996 Israeli legislative election which took place on 29 May 1996 and were the first Israeli elections in which Israelis elected their prime minister directly.
